name: pos
author: ServeOS
//electron: Pinned exactly, not a ^ range: npm workspaces hoist electron to the repo root, electron-builder only looks in apps/pos/node_modules, and its fallback of reading the declared version needs that version to be fixed (electron-builder#3984). A range here fails the packaging step with 'Cannot compute electron version'. Bump it deliberately.
//scripts: The tsc step in `build` is --noEmit on purpose: it is a typecheck gate, and vite-plugin-electron — not tsc — produces the dist-electron/{main,preload}.js that actually ship. Letting it emit wrote dist-electron/_offline/*.test.js, which vitest then collected as CommonJS test files and failed on (its exclude covers electron/_offline, not dist-electron/_offline), and shipped the parked offline tests inside the installer.

scripts.build: tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json && vite build && electron-builder --publish never

//: better-sqlite3 is parked with the offline store in electron/_offline; kept optional so a failed native build never blocks `npm install`. (Note lives at top level — npm rejects a '//' comment key inside a dependencies object with EINVALIDPACKAGENAME, which breaks install/CI and Vercel deploys.)
//build: Notes on the `build` block below — they live out here because electron-builder validates its config against a schema and rejects unknown keys, so a '//' inside it fails the build. (1) `files` ships only the two bundles: vite emits the renderer to dist/, vite-plugin-electron emits main+preload to dist-electron/, and apps/pos has no runtime dependencies — everything is bundled. (2) better-sqlite3 is excluded and npmRebuild is off because it is an optionalDependency of the parked offline store with zero live imports; letting electron-builder collect it would bundle a native binding built for Node, not Electron. Both come back when the offline engine is unparked. (3) `mac.identity: null` makes the unsigned build explicit rather than accidental — signing needs an Apple Developer cert, and without one macOS Gatekeeper requires right-click - Open on first launch. It is paired with the `afterPack` hook, which ad-hoc signs the bundle: skipping signing entirely leaves the Electron binary's own linker signature over a resource set packaging has changed, which fails `codesign --verify` and gets the download refused as 'damaged' — a wall right-click - Open does not get past. See build/adhoc-sign-mac.mjs. (4) `artifactName` overrides the default, which interpolates productName and would put a space in every filename — that breaks the unquoted glob the release workflow passes to `gh release create`, and turns every download URL into %20 soup. (5) Two icon masters, generated from src/app/icon.svg by build/render-icon.mjs: macOS gets the inset one because the platform adds no padding of its own, Windows gets full-bleed because it draws .ico into a tile it owns. electron-builder derives .icns and .ico from these PNGs. (6) `publish` does not make the build publish anything — the build script passes --publish never, and the workflow uploads assets itself. It is here because it is what makes electron-builder emit latest-mac.yml / latest.yml and embed app-update.yml in the bundle; electron-updater reads those to discover releases, and without this block auto-update has nothing to look at.
//electron-updater: A devDependency, not a dependency, and deliberately so: apps/pos ships zero runtime node_modules — vite bundles the renderer and vite-plugin-electron rollups the main process, which is why `files` can list two directories and nothing else. Making it a real dependency would ask electron-builder to collect it out of the workspace-hoisted root node_modules, the same resolution path that already breaks for electron itself. Bundling keeps the installer self-contained. Same reason react and react-dom sit in devDependencies.
